newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn improves Hermes export insurance programme.
newsitem.headline: Bonn improves Hermes export insurance programme.

text.p: The German government has improved its Hermes export insurance programme, improving competitive conditions for small and medium-sized enterprises in particular, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
The plan has been upgraded in line with standards in other western countries so that Hermes will now be able to repay exporters sooner in the event of a payment problem, the ministry said.
For finance credits with five-percent self-financing, repayment should take place within two months and one week, instead of six months as had been the case.
For contracts with foreign private customers, deductibles will be reduced to 15 percent from 25 percent, it said.
Members of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) are increasingly likely to agree a standardisation of export insurance premiums.
This would eliminate one of the biggest reasons for competitive disadvantage, it said.
